title: Implement CD Command
goal: Change the current working directory of premium shell process directly.

narrative.hook: Your shell can execute external programs and wait for them to finish, but every command runs inside its own isolated child process.
narrative.motivation: If you try to change directories using an external program, only that temporary child process updates its location while your main shell stays completely stationary.
narrative.concrete_demo: Typing a directory-navigation instruction needs to update the active environment of your main process so that subsequent inputs execute inside the newly selected folder.

learning_objectives: Understand how a process maintains its working directory as part of its execution state.
Recognize why directory-changing instructions must be handled internally instead of spawning external binaries.
Learn how to invoke the system facility that updates the current working directory.
constraints: Must not spawn an external child process for the directory change instruction.
Must modify the execution state of the current shell process directly.
Must handle standard path arguments correctly.
deliverables: An internal directory-updating routine that modifies the current working directory state.

behaviors.description: The shell intercepts directory-change instructions and updates its working directory state directly.

tests.description: Verifies that supplying a valid target path updates the working directory successfully.
tests.expected_behavior: The directory updates correctly without spawning external tools.

tests.description: Verifies behavior when supplying an invalid or nonexistent target path.
tests.expected_behavior: The directory remains unchanged and an error indicator is reported.

tests.description: Dynamic verification of directory navigation across multiple sequential steps.
tests.expected_behavior: Sequential path changes update state accurately.
